Definition: from G303 and the base of G43; constraint (literally or figuratively); by implication, distress:--distress, must needs, (of) necessity(-sary), needeth, needful.
BiblicalUsage: Paul says necessity is laid upon him — woe unto me if I preach not the gospel — and he takes pleasure in necessities, in distresses for Christ's sake, for when he is weak then he is strong. Jesus warns of great distress in the land in the days to come, and Hebrews says that when the priesthood is changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law. The word is constraint, distress, the thing that must be: the pressure that drives the preacher, the trouble that proves the apostle, and the necessity that changes the priesthood.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe necessity is the pressure that shows what a man is made of: Paul preached because he must, and he took pleasure in the necessities because they proved Christ's strength in his weakness. And I hold that the greatest necessity in the Bible is the one in Hebrews — the priesthood had to change, because the old one could not finish the work, and the new Priest could.
